analysis.Alignment, Safety & Governance (A): Not addressed; the paper focuses on personalization attributes without discussion of safety tuning, red-teaming, or governance aspects like refusal training or watermarking.
analysis.Evaluation & Benchmarks (E): Experiments on MBTI personality and Role-Playing benchmarks demonstrate effectiveness with up to 16-18% improvements, involving domain-specific evaluations but not adversarial or calibration tests.
analysis.Optimization & Training Recipe (R): No training or optimization recipes are discussed, as the approach is decoding-time only and requires no extra training, optimizers, or parallelism strategies.
analysis.Objectives & Learning Signals (O): No new training objectives or losses are introduced; the method leverages implicit density ratios from pre-trained single-dimensional models for decoding-time sampling, without involving pretraining losses or preference learning.
analysis.Data & Inputs (I): The paper utilizes datasets for MBTI personality and Role-Playing in experiments, but does not focus on data curation, tokenization, or multimodal alignment; data is primarily for evaluation rather than model inputs during pretraining.

title: LGCC: Enhancing Flow Matching Based Text-Guided Image Editing with Local Gaussian Coupling and Context Consistency

analysis.Inference & Systems (S): The paper focuses on inference efficiency, achieving 3x-5x speedup for lightweight editing and 2x for universal editing, with reduced inference steps and 40%-50% of the inference time of BAGEL or Flux.
analysis.Architecture & Modeling (M): The paper introduces LGCC with Local Gaussian Noise Coupling (LGNC) to model coupled target image embeddings and Content Consistency Loss (CCL) for semantic alignment, enhancing flow matching-based MLLM architecture for detail preservation.
analysis.Alignment, Safety & Governance (A): No aspects of alignment, safety, or governance are discussed; the abstract focuses on editing quality and efficiency without mention of ethical safeguards or policy enforcement.
analysis.Evaluation & Benchmarks (E): Evaluation uses I2EBench, reporting improvements in local detail scores (1.60%) and overall scores (0.53%), with comparisons to BAGEL and Flux on speed and quality metrics.
analysis.Optimization & Training Recipe (R): Curriculum learning is used to integrate LGCC with the pre-trained BAGEL model, indicating a structured training approach for stable fine-tuning and component integration.
analysis.Objectives & Learning Signals (O): Content Consistency Loss (CCL) is proposed as a learning signal to ensure semantic alignment between edit instructions and image modifications, preventing unintended content removal and addressing inconsistency.
analysis.Data & Inputs (I): The paper does not explicitly discuss data inputs; it builds on the pre-trained BAGEL model, implying reliance on existing data pipelines without introducing new data processing methods.

title: In Good GRACEs: Principled Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation

analysis.Inference & Systems (S): Inference and serving systems are not discussed; the paper focuses on training-time teacher selection for distillation efficiency, not batching, quantization, or decoding methods.
analysis.Architecture & Modeling (M): No novel architectures are proposed; the work relies on existing foundation models like LLaMA and OLMo for teacher-student distillation without modifying backbone designs or attention mechanisms.
analysis.Alignment, Safety & Governance (A): Alignment, safety, and governance are not addressed; evaluations are on task performance without red-teaming, refusal training, or harm-related constraints.
analysis.Evaluation & Benchmarks (E): Strong evaluation on reasoning benchmarks GSM8K and MATH, with Spearman correlation up to 86% and performance gains up to 7.4%, focusing on distillation effectiveness without calibration or adversarial tests.

analysis.Objectives & Learning Signals (O): Knowledge distillation employs standard objectives, but the paper does not introduce new losses; GRACE scores gradient properties to guide teacher selection, not learning signal design.
analysis.Data & Inputs (I): The paper uses data generated by teacher models for distillation but does not detail raw corpora, tokenization, or data processing methods; it focuses on generated outputs from teachers without specifying sources or augmentation.
